rows.note: Use 新 as the all-purpose adjective for things recently made, unused, newly discovered, newly born, newly introduced or not previously known, and newly begun.

example.jyutping: nei1 bou6 sau2 gei1 hai6 san1 maai5 ge3

rows.note: Use 陌生 for the slice of “new” meaning strange or unfamiliar, rather than merely recently introduced.

example.english: I met them for the first time, and they felt new to me.
example.traditional: 我第一次見佢，覺得好陌生。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dai6 jat1 ci3 gin3 keoi5 gok3 dak1 hou2 maak6 sang1

rows.note: Use 新嚟嘅 for a person who has recently arrived or joined a place, such as a new classmate or colleague.

example.english: That new colleague still doesn't know the way around.
example.traditional: 嗰個新嚟嘅同事仲未識路。
example.jyutping: go2 go3 san1 lei4 ge3 tung4 si6 zung6 mei6 sik1 lou6

rows.note: Use 唔熟手 when someone is inexperienced or not yet accustomed to doing a particular task.

example.english: When I first worked on this machine, I was still new at it.
example.traditional: 我初初整呢部機，仲好唔熟手。
example.jyutping: ngo5 co1 co1 zing2 ni1 bou6 gei1 zung6 hou2 m4 suk6 sau2
